{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZdy8qw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhDE-gY", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 93, "title": "Add a browser-local outbound Internet-mail journey using INET# addressing", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `33ae49b4b4aa1acccb1614a6c81fa86b864f008c`, electronic mail cannot represent an Internet destination despite contemporary documentation of that capability.

With a local human handle selected, enter MAIN `1` and try `WRITE INET#observer@letters.example.invalid`. `src/commands.ts:172` resolves the destination exclusively through `resolveMailResident`; the address is rejected. `createHumanMail` repeats that restriction, and `validateMailRelations` requires a known human/resident pair. SENT and READ consequently have no external-address representation.

This is an existing fidelity gap. Earlier mail scopes explicitly deferred Internet mail.

## Expected outcome

Enable this browser-local journey:

`mail entry → discover an original fictional Internet address → WRITE INET#address → compose → review/edit → explicit local submission or cancellation → SENT/READ → reload and backup/restore`

Preserve the Internet address as an address, independently of local resident identities. Explain concisely that submission saves the letter in this browser and sends nothing to an email server. Do not fabricate delivery, receipt, replies or recipient-read evidence.

Extend the existing shared mailbox projection through MAIN `1`, MAIN `X` and SIG `MAIL`, preserving their distinct entry and return contexts. Their historical equivalence remains an existing reconstruction assumption.

## Context

Historical sources were inspected live on 2026-10-24:

- [Internet Magazine, November 1996, printed p. 221](https://iwparchives.jp/wp-content/themes/twentytwelve/bn/pdf/im199611-220-mail2.pdf) explicitly specifies the PC-VAN `INET#` destination prefix. Confidence is high for target-year addressing. Its binary-conversion information does not require attachments or historical size limits in this text-only increment. PDF text was readable; page-image retrieval failed.
- [Internet Magazine, October 1994, printed pp. 106–107](https://iwparchives.jp/wp-content/themes/twentytwelve/bn/pdf/im199410-104-bbs.pdf) independently explains that prefix and distinguishes Internet destinations from intra-service IDs. Confidence is high within its earlier period; the November 1996 source supplies target-year corroboration. Its illustrated NIFTY-Serve composition controls must remain separate.
- [Use of Commercial Networks, January 1994, pp. 297–300](https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/agrmet1943/49/4/49_4_297/_pdf) preserves earlier WIDENET/X.400 routing and `INET#` examples. Extraction is badly damaged. Those earlier gateway stages do not establish the 1996 host-mail route and are not implementation requirements.

Focused searches did not recover a qualifying complete 1996 host-composition or current/old-mail transition sequence. The [computer-history preservation page](https://elestamp.o.oo7.jp/Computer_history.htm) returned 403; its indexed ECOM material was not used to specify private-mail controls. Accessible publisher sources support proceeding without that page.

**Accepted reconstruction:** retain the app's existing WRITE/COMPOSE, editor, review and cancellation conventions. Address-validation limits, local storage, status wording and screen placement are category D product choices, not authenticated host behavior. Use an original `example.invalid` address in discoverable mail help; this is a modern fictional-example convention. No historical identities, messages or contact directory should be copied.

Implementation precedents are `src/composer.ts`, `src/mail.ts`, `src/storage/repository.ts:createHumanMail`, and existing mail repository/browser tests. `src/ai/mail.ts:pairMail` currently restricts resident memory to correspondent pairs; preserve that isolation when introducing external destinations.

Live searches found no open Issues or PRs. [#83](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/83) excludes Internet-mail implementation; [#89](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/89) excludes Internet-mail delivery. This advances those deferred boundaries and the working local-operation convention of [#33](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/33).

[PR #92](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/pull/92) and `docs/validation.md` report 322 passing checks, configured type checking/build and OSL browser-download validation. These are recorded Coordinator results, not checks run by this research graph, and do not validate this proposed increment.

Scope is outbound plain-text composition and durable local inspection. Inbound Internet mail, mailbox migration, remote transport, attachments, multiple recipients, delivery simulation and exact historical editor reconstruction remain deferred.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Accept explicit `INET#address` destinations through both direct WRITE/COMPOSE and the existing omitted-address prompt. Provide discoverable syntax and one original fictional example without registering an external correspondent as a member. Preserve local stable-address precedence and ambiguous-handle rejection. Explicit Internet destinations must never silently resolve to residents.
- [ ] Define and document a bounded single-address ASCII subset suitable for ordinary examples. Preserve accepted address spelling and case through opening, review, persistence, SENT, READ and restore. Reject malformed, empty, multiple-recipient, control-containing and unsupported forms consistently in controller, repository and import validation. Validation limits are reconstructed, not historical claims; full email-standard support is unnecessary.
- [ ] Reuse the existing literal Japanese composer, editing, explicit review approval and cancellation behavior. Pin the destination through editing and save retry. External opening/review and success output clearly identify browser-local saving with no actual transmission. Do not reuse an unqualified remote-delivery success claim for this branch.
- [ ] Add the smallest explicit external-destination representation within the existing mail/backup architecture. Require a valid existing human sender and exactly one destination kind. Do not weaken legacy resident correspondence, parent or confirmation validation. External records cannot carry resident simulation, human-recipient read markers, recipient confirmation or reply relationships unsupported by this outbound scope. Reject contradictory and forged variants on writes and imports.
- [ ] Preserve atomic record/number allocation, monotonic numbering and idempotent retries. Concurrent identical submissions create one letter; an ID collision with different content or destination fails. Quota/transaction failure retains a retryable draft without a partial record or consumed number. A committed save consumes the draft even if subsequent refresh fails.
- [ ] SENT and READ display the external destination and truthful local-save status. External letters remain absent from INBOX and other local humans' mailbox projections. They do not acquire synthetic member tokens, remote read status or generated replies. Preserve local identity/name rendering, human read markers and explicit-parent resident confirmation unchanged.
- [ ] Keep external addresses, subjects and bodies outside resident pair memory, generation targets and forum/OLT prompts. External letters must not create resident acquaintance or consume resident correspondence limits. Preserve consent, scheduling and context boundaries. No network request, mailto handoff, address lookup or model loading is caused by this journey.
- [ ] Extend existing Playwright coverage for address parsing/preservation, strict imported variants, local/external mixed numbering, concurrent/idempotent saves, quota rollback, SENT/READ, reload and JSON round-trip. Exercise a production keyboard journey with Japanese multiline literal text, review/EDIT, explicit approval and cancellation; check the other two mail routes and contextual returns. Include existing simulated-IME protection, reset/restore invalidation and request observation. Preserve existing functional, storage, consent, private-context, IME and terminal regression coverage; retain meaningful rejection tests while updating the newly supported address case.
- [ ] Update `docs/mail.md`, applicable storage documentation, the historical research record and relevant README/Settings/About descriptions. Record source dates, URLs, confidence and reconstruction assumptions, including unresolved mailbox relationships. Document external-letter inclusion in backups/logs. Keep ordinary terminal explanation concise and detailed provenance on existing documentation/About surfaces.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs documented `npm test`, whose configured servers include TypeScript checking and production bundling, and records actual results and any failures. Review the complete diff, documentation links and `git diff --check`. Use existing tooling and deterministic fixtures or mocked inference; no new framework, real model or human/hardware gate is required.

## Optional validation

Additional browser-engine coverage or a newly recovered dated host transcript may refine compatibility or historical presentation. Neither is a completion gate.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. All acceptance checks can be completed before merge.
